questions.question: Which features go in the purchases block's single paid-feature list for the starter, given each app will replace it?
questions.default: Ship a one-entry placeholder list ["pro-example"] gated by the "pro" entitlement, for each app to replace.

questions.question: What minimum free space should the storage block keep before refusing a write with "not-enough-space", when the app sets no limit?
What are the RevenueCat public SDK keys (iOS and Android) for the sandbox project with the "pro" entitlement, to be set as EXPO_PUBLIC values in the development EAS environment?
questions.default: Build and test against the fake and the missing-key path (price returns null); Block Lab purchase checks stay failing until the keys are set.

questions.question: block.json needs keys for the EXPO_PUBLIC values and the device checks. The tests use "env" (a list of EXPO_PUBLIC_* names) and "deviceChecks" (each a string or { name }). Do you want different key names?
questions.default: Use the keys name, packages, env and deviceChecks.

questions.question: Each block's config.js is CommonJS and exports parts of an Expo config: plugins, ios.infoPlist for permission texts, and ios.privacyManifests.NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes. app.config.ts merges these for every folder present. Should Android permissions (android.permissions) be part of this contract too?
questions.default: Only plugins, iOS infoPlist permission texts and iOS privacy manifest entries are required. Android permissions come through each block's config plugins.

questions.question: With the fakes switch on, the test requires index.ts and index.web.ts to export every name fake.ts exports, as the same value. Until the first real block exists, that test checks nothing real, so F002 can pass it without any block. Should F002 ship a sample block so the switch is tested from the start?
questions.default: No sample block. The switch test starts checking real blocks when the first block feature (storage, R-003) lands.

questions.question: The imaging block is marked as not needing a device, so the tests expect it to decode and encode images in JavaScript. That will be slow on full phone-camera photos (roughly seconds per page). Should R-007 instead need a device and use a native library such as Skia, with device checks in the Block Lab?
questions.default: Keep it in JavaScript (no device needed): filters, crop, split and stack write PNG, and resize writes JPEG.

questions.question: Is an empty-string password treated as 'no password' or as a password shorter than 4 characters (an error)?
questions.default: Treat an empty-string password as not covered by the tests; the implementation may treat it as no password.

questions.question: What page size does write use when no pageSize is given?
questions.default: The tests always pass pageSize when size matters; the default is left to the implementation (auto is suggested).

questions.question: Does "6 GB of memory" mean 6 GiB (6×2^30 bytes) as reported by expo-device totalMemory, given that 6 GB phones often report a little less than that?
questions.default: Tests only require 6 GiB and above to be "downloadable" and 4 GiB and below to be "unavailable"; the exact threshold between is left to the implementation.

questions.question: Should a failed download resolve { error: <code> } (not throw), and should a cancelled download resolve { error: "cancelled" } specifically?
questions.default: Yes: failures resolve { error: <any string> } and a cancel resolves { error: "cancelled" }, following the SPEC rule that blocks return error codes for expected outcomes.

questions.question: Does "larger than 200 MB" mean more than 200,000,000 bytes (decimal) or more than 200 × 1,048,576 bytes (binary)?
questions.default: Decimal (200,000,000 bytes). The tests use 150 MB and 2 GB, so either reading passes.

questions.question: translate() resolves a string for success, so the tests expect a language not yet downloaded to resolve { error: "needs-download" } rather than the bare string "needs-download", which could be mistaken for a translation. Is that what you want?
questions.default: translate resolves { error: "needs-download" }, and on web { error: "not-available" }. downloadLanguage resolves the bare strings "downloaded" or "declined".

questions.question: The tests expect the phone's recognizer and translator to be reached through requireOptionalNativeModule("TextRecognizer") (recognizeAsync(uri) returns lines with pixel frames, in no set order) and requireOptionalNativeModule("Translator") (languagesAsync, translateAsync(text, code), and downloadAsync(code), which returns a boolean). The block sorts the lines by frame. Should this block use a packaged library such as ML Kit instead of custom bridges?
questions.default: Custom native bridges with these names and methods, built in the native session. A missing module reads as "not-available".

questions.question: Does "empty text" include text that is only whitespace, and does it apply to recognize at all (for example, an empty image path)?
questions.default: The tests only check translate("") → "" with no native calls. Whitespace-only text and recognize inputs are left to the implementation.
